From: Connor Leigh <connor@battenhealth.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-02T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Initial ask: catalog-level model affinity & audit tagging (priority)

Olga —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Batten Health is preparing the SOW and they have two blocking requirements for GA that we need to surface as a hard ask to product/eng:

1) Per-catalog model affinity: customers need the ability to pin particular model variants to specific catalog routes (not just tenant-wide). This is to ensure our clinical summaries use the validated model.
2) Audit tags on inference: every response must include a stable audit tag (model id + quantization profile + runtime kernel id) surfaced in trace logs and in the API response headers for compliance.

These are deal breakers for Batten’s procurement/security team. They are asking for an estimate and whether this can be delivered in the next 6 weeks for their pilot start. I attached the SOW draft and the completed security questionnaire for background.

Connor
Director of AI Integrations
Batten Health

Attachments: Batten_SOW_draft.pdf, security_questionnaire_completed.xlsx

Thanks for flagging, Olga. I reviewed the SOW and questionnaire. High-level thoughts:

- Per-catalog model affinity: product has a roadmap item for "route affinity" but it's scoped for Q1 next year because it touches routing policy, rollout, and our model catalog UI. The feature surface is non-trivial: it requires changes to the routing layer + API to accept route-level descriptors and the console to express them.

- Audit tags on inference: we already include kernel/runtime metadata in internal traces, but we do not currently surface a stable, customer-consumable audit tag in API responses. That is feasible with a small API addition + trace propagation change.

Options to unblock deal quickly:
1) Fast path (2–3 sprints): Expose a compact audit tag in API headers and include it in exported traces. This is lower risk and we can scope it for a two-sprint fast track if eng prioritizes.
2) Workaround for model affinity (short-term): Add a config-level "route override" (operator-only) that maps route-name -> model-variant for a small set of routes. This would be an operational shim and not public UI. Effort ~3 sprints with a small ops playbook.
3) Full solution (Q1): proper route affinity, UI, and rollout semantics.

We need eng estimates for options 1 and 2. If Ben/Olga want to push on Q4 commitment, we should be explicit on tradeoffs. I can draft a short PRD and can link the internal design doc (PRD-921).

Marissa
Director, Product Management | Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Fwd: Initial ask: catalog-level model affinity & audit tagging (priority)

Quick engineering take after reviewing the questionnaire and Marissa's options: 

- Audit tag exposure (Option 1): Low complexity. We can add a short, stable header (X-Redwood-AuditTag) that contains model_id|quant_profile|kernel_id. Work items: API header plumbing, trace exporter change, and docs. Estimated effort: 5 engineering story points (~1 sprint including QA). No infra changes required.

- Route override shim (Option 2): Medium complexity. Build an operator-only routing table read at service start that maps catalog-route -> model-id. This avoids touching the UI and rollout system. Caveats: requires operator coordination for updates, and doesn't support gradual rollouts. Estimated effort: 12 story points (~2–3 sprints). Needs an ops playbook for updates and a migration path to the full solution.

Constraints & risks:
- 6-week deadline is tight if we want both items in production. We can deliver the audit header inside one sprint and the shim in two additional sprints if prioritized (requires 3-sprint commitment).
- Security: the audit header is minimal risk, but we should ensure PII is not included. PRD-921 and the security questionnaire look fine; I attached a short risk note.

Recommendation: ship audit-tag header as a must-have for the pilot. Offer the route override shim as a managed, time-boxed engineering project. If sales needs a GA commitment for full route affinity, we should cap the date to Q1 and mark feature gating accordingly.

Jordan
Staff Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

Attachments: engineering_risk_notes.md
